result.title: Configuring RAG Systems: What Breaks, Where Originates, and How to Fix
result.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant paradigm for improving Large Language Model (LLM) by intertwining it with other components, such as a vector/graph database. Therefore, the resulting RAG systems are often highly configurable, under which a non-trivial amount of failures are related to the configurations. However, there remains a lack of systematic understanding regarding the configuration issues for RAG systems. To bridge this gap, in this paper, we conduct the first large-scale empirical study of 654 real-world configuration issues collected from 10 diverse RAG systems. Drawing on this, we provide a complete categorization of the symptoms, root causes, relevant stages, and fix patterns of configuration issues for RAG systems, as well as several new observations. Our findings not only reveal the characteristics of configuration issues, but also strongly link them to the unique pipeline stages of RAG, e.g., we found that most symptoms can be observed at the early or late stage, while the stage of the root cause might not be at the same stage as where the symptom is identified. We also provide nine actionable insights to the practitioners on testing, localizing, and fixing the configuration issues for RAG systems.

AI.relevance_reason: 该文是对 10 个 RAG 系统 654 个配置问题的实证归类（症状、根因、阶段与修复模式），属软件工程与系统运维范畴；虽提及「症状与根因可能不在同一流水线阶段」这一观察，但讨论对象是配置参数与系统故障，未涉及内部推理状态的表示、生成、证据使用或停止决策，也未提供可供迁移的方法线索，故不入选。
